text: None of them knew the color of the sky, for their eyes stayed fixed on the waves that swept toward them across the gray sea. <break time="0.8s" /> The waves were the color of slate, except for their tops, which were foaming white, and every man in the boat knew the colors of the sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Many a man owns a bathtub larger than the little dinghy, which rose and fell on each wave like a wild horse. <break time="0.8s" /> The cook sat in the bottom of the boat, bailing out the water, his eyes fixed on the thin edge that separated him from the ocean. <break time="0.8s" /> The oiler and the correspondent each pulled an oar, and in the bow lay the captain, who had been hurt when the ship went down. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain was sad and quiet, for he had seen his ship sink, and a captain never forgets the loss of his ship. <break time="0.8s" /> We are not far from the house of refuge near Mosquito Inlet Light, said the cook, and they will pick us up as soon as they see us. <break time="0.8s" /> But the correspondent replied that houses of refuge had no crews, for they were only places where food and clothes were stored. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, we are not there yet, said the oiler, and the argument ended, the men turning their eyes back to the waves.
